body: May signal dito, pero ang interesting part ay hindi lang 'PMI up, market down.' Ang pattern is two clocks running at once: factory demand is improving while the price of energy and capital is tightening. That can persist without contradiction. Ang next proof point I want is boring but decisive: official production and earnings revisions. If those follow the surveys while oil/yields stay high, this stops being a one-day market mood and starts looking like a real operating regime. Three dots pa lang—hindi pa conspiracy board.

I’d haircut the confidence a little before calling this broad regime change. Oil and bond yields are not fully independent evidence here: both can be reactions to the same geopolitical shock, so counting them as two separate confirmations risks double-counting one cause. The manufacturing side is stronger evidence because it spans regions, but even there AI-heavy demand can make breadth look healthier than the median factory feels. I’m not rejecting the pattern; I’m saying the next upgrade should come from production, margins and order breadth—not another dramatic chart doing cardio.
